title: Artin approximation by an etale local algebra
statement: Let A be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let p be a prime ideal of A [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and let f_1, ..., f_m be polynomials in A[x_1, ..., x_n]. Suppose that (a_1, ..., a_n) is a solution of all f_j=0 in the maximal-ideal completion of A_p [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. If A_p is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], then for every integer N>=1 there exist an etale ring map A to A', a prime ideal p' of A' lying over p, and a solution (b_1, ..., b_n) in A' of all f_j=0 such that the residue-field map kappa(p) to kappa(p') is an isomorphism and a_i-b_i belongs to (p')^N times the maximal-ideal completion of A'_{p'} for every i.

source.place: Tag 0CAR, lemma-approximation-property-variant (Smoothing Ring Maps, Section 07XA), statement and proof.

proof.text: Put $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pR$, and $H=\widehat R$. Localization preserves Noetherianity, and completion preserves Noetherianity, so both $R$ and $H$ are Noetherian. The G-ring hypothesis and the completion-regularity theorem make $R\to H$ regular. Popescu therefore presents $H$ as a colimit of a small filtered diagram of smooth $R$-algebras $B_j$, with $R$-algebra coprojections.

Regard each $f_j$ as a polynomial over $R$ and set $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$. Evaluation at the given tuple defines an $R$-algebra map $v:P\to H$, since every relation evaluates to zero. The finite-presentation factorization theorem supplies a stage $B$ and maps $P\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{w}H$ with $wu=v$. Thus, for $z_i=u(x_i)$, one has $f_j(z)=0$ in $B$ and $w(z_i)=a_i$. The affine morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth by the conclusion of the Popescu presentation in step 1.

source.place: Proof of Tag 07QZ, smooth factorization; Tags 00QO (lemma-characterize-finite-presentation) and 07C3 (lemma-when-colimit)

proof.text: Fix $N\ge1$. Every ideal of $R$ is finitely generated, in particular $\mathfrak m$. Reduction of the completion gives an $R$-algebra map $\pi_N:H\to R/\mathfrak m^N$ whose kernel is $\mathfrak m^NH$. Apply smooth-section lifting to $\sigma=\pi_Nw:B\to R/\mathfrak m^N$, with ideal exactly $\mathfrak m^N$. It gives an etale $R$-algebra $E$, an isomorphism $\alpha:R/\mathfrak m^N\xrightarrow{\sim}E/\mathfrak m^NE$, and an $R$-algebra map $t:B\to E$ satisfying $q_Nt=\alpha\sigma$. Put $c_i=t(z_i)$. Polynomial evaluation commutes with $t$, so $f_j(c)=0$, and $q_N(c_i)=\alpha\pi_N(a_i)$.

source.place: Tag 07M7 (lemma-lift-section-smooth-morphism) applied with I=m^N; algebra.tex Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated)

proof.text: Reducing $\alpha$ further modulo $\mathfrak m$ gives $E/\mathfrak mE\cong R/\mathfrak m=k$. Consequently $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak mE$ is a maximal ideal, lies over $\mathfrak m$, and its residue field is $k$. Put $T=E_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qT=\mathfrak mT$. The map $R\to T$ is local and $\mathfrak n$ is finitely generated by the images of generators of $\mathfrak m$. Take the induced map $\widehat R\to\widehat T$ of local completions. Choose $r_i\in R$ representing $\pi_N(a_i)$. Step 3 says $c_i-r_i\in\mathfrak m^NE$, hence $c_i-r_i\in\mathfrak n^N$ in $T$. Compatibility of the completion map with the $N$th coordinates says the images of $a_i$ and $r_i$ have the same $N$th coordinate in $\widehat T$. Therefore the $N$th coordinate of $a_i-c_i$ in $\widehat T$ is zero. The kernel formula for completion modulo powers, now applied to $(T,\mathfrak n)$, gives $a_i-c_i\in\mathfrak n^N\widehat T$.

source.place: Tag 07QZ, residue field and congruence conclusion; algebra.tex Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated); more-algebra.tex Tag 07ED

proof.text: Apply the unpointed etale algebra model at a prime to $A$, $\mathfrak p$, and the etale $A_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra $E$. It supplies an etale $A$-algebra $C$, an $A$-algebra map $i:C\to E$, and a multiplicative subset $M\subset C$ such that $E=M^{-1}C$. The structure equation in that statement identifies $A\to C\to E$ with $A\to R\to E$. In particular contraction of $\mathfrak q$ to $A$ is $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 00U2 (lemma-etale), (10); used in proof of smoothing.tex Tag 0CAR

proof.text: Write the finitely many elements $c_i\in M^{-1}C$ as $u_i/s_i$ with $s_i\in M$. Put $h_0=\prod_i s_i\in M$ (empty product $1$). In $C_{h_0}$ all $s_i$ are invertible, so $d_i=u_i/s_i$ is defined and maps to $c_i$. Each of the finitely many elements $f_j(d)$ maps to zero in $M^{-1}C$. The fraction equality defining localization gives $v_j\in M$ with $v_jf_j(d)=0$ in $C_{h_0}$: for a representative $f_j(d)=e_j/h_0^{r_j}$, its zero image means some $v_j\in M$ kills $e_j$ in $C$. Set $h=h_0\prod_jv_j\in M$ and $A'=C_h$. Then $b_i=d_i|_{C_h}$ satisfies every $f_j(b)=0$ exactly, and maps to $c_i$ in $E$.

source.place: Tag 0CAR (lemma-approximation-property-variant), clearing denominators in its proof; algebra.tex Tag 00CO (definition-localization)

proof.text: The principal-localization map $\operatorname{Spec}C_h\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is an open immersion, hence etale. Its composite with the etale map $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale. Thus $A\to A'$ has the required etaleness.

Let $\mathfrak r=i^{-1}(\mathfrak q)\subset C$. Every element of $M$ maps to a unit of $E$, so $M\cap\mathfrak r=\varnothing$ and $h\notin\mathfrak r$. Let $\mathfrak p'$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak q$ under $A'=C_h\to E$; it is prime and contracts to $\mathfrak p$ in $A$. There is a canonical $A$-algebra isomorphism $A'_{\mathfrak p'}\cong E_{\mathfrak q}=T$: both sides are $C_{\mathfrak r}$. Explicitly, an element $x/s\in M^{-1}C$ is outside $\mathfrak q$ exactly when $x\notin\mathfrak r$, so localizing it at $\mathfrak q$ inverts exactly the remaining numerators outside $\mathfrak r$; the same argument applies to $C_h$. These inverse fraction maps identify maximal ideals and induce coordinatewise isomorphisms on their completion towers. Thus the residue map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is the isomorphism $k\to T/\mathfrak n$ from step 4. They carry $b_i$ to $c_i$ and the canonical completion map from $\widehat R$ to the one used in step 4. Its congruence becomes $a_i-b_i\in(\mathfrak p')^N\widehat{A'_{\mathfrak p'}}$, as required.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q12-adc14c5d3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read every part of the delivery. The item statement matches Stacks 0CAR (smoothing.tex l.3347) hypothesis by hypothesis: A is Noetherian, p is any prime, f_j are in A[x], the solution is in (A_p)^, and A_p is a G-ring. The conclusion is étale A->A', a prime p' over p with trivial residue extension, a solution b, and a-b in p'^N (A'_{p'})^. The only difference is N>=1 instead of every integer N, and N<=0 is trivial. The statement was not changed. Step 1: the localization and completion Noetherian nodes, the G-ring completion-regular node and Popescu are each used with exactly their hypotheses. Step 2: the finite-presentation filtered-colimit factorization gives f(z)=0 in a smooth B. Step 3: I checked 07M7 (more-algebra l.2139). Its ideal is arbitrary and it assumes no henselianity, so lifting modulo m^N is legitimate. q_N(c)=alpha pi_N(a) and f(c)=0. Step 4: E/mE=k makes q maximal. n=mT is finitely generated, so the kernel formula 05GG applies to (T,n) without a Noetherian claim on T. The induced completion map is followed at the Nth coordinate, which gives a-c in n^N T^. Step 5: the étale-algebra model is used by its statement only (C, i, M-localization, structure equation). Step 6: an elementary clearing of the denominators s_i and the equation errors v_j. It works with zero divisors. Step 7: open immersion plus composition gives étaleness. Step 8: an elementary identification A'_{p'}=C_r=E_q as A-algebras. It carries the residue map, b_i->c_i and the canonical completion map, so the congruence is the required one. Edge cases checked: N=1, m=0, no variables or equations, non-reduced A, the zero ring. There are no new nodes. I found no duplicate by grep for 0CAR, 07QZ and Artin approximation or G-ring wording, or by blueprint_refs search. The dependency closure of 970 nodes is acyclic, and no SGA source is used. I accept all 11 declared tool_uses as generic algebra black boxes for the recorded 0CAR input. Side note, not a fault of this delivery: the existing node lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-completion-map-local cites Tag 07ED, whose label is formally-smooth-completion. No fixes were written.
